intro: Agentry opens and follows GitHub's pull requests (#12) and GitLab's merge requests (!12) with the gh and glab programs on this machine. It stores no key: it uses the session each program already has.

row.checking: Reading the version and the hosts…

reason.version-untested: It works, but {{version}} is newer than {{recorded}}, the latest Agentry has been tested with.
reason.below-minimum: {{version}} is older than {{minimum}}, the oldest release Agentry works with.
reason.no-hosts: {{cli}} is installed, but not signed in to any host.
reason.signed-out: {{cli}} is installed, but not signed in to any host.
reason.not-installed: {{cli}} is not installed, or Agentry cannot find it.
reason.probe-failed: {{cli}} did not answer the way Agentry expects.
reason.timeout: {{cli}} did not answer in time, so Agentry stopped it.
reason.disabled: Agentry does not use it while it is off. Projects on its hosts cannot open requests.

bin.title: {{cli}} binary
bin.hint: Agentry uses this program instead of searching the PATH. Before saving it, it reads its version and checks it is not older than {{minimum}}.
bin.absolute: Enter an absolute path, starting with /.
bin.cleared: {{cli}} now uses the one on PATH

empty.title: Agentry cannot find gh or glab
empty.body: Without one of them it cannot open pull requests or merge requests. Install it and it will show up here by itself, with no need to check again.

missing.text: Missing a host? Sign in to it with the program that fits and it will show up here by itself.
missing.link: How to sign in to another host

tracker.title: Issue trackers
tracker.note: Agentry imports issues from GitHub Issues (#12) and GitLab Issues (#12) with the same programs it already uses for pull requests and merge requests, and from YouTrack (PROJ-12) with JetBrains' youtrack-app and the address and token you give it below.

reason.ready: Reads and writes issues with {{cli}}, with the session it already has. It works in projects whose code is on {{host}}.
reason.disabled: Agentry does not use {{tracker}} while it is off.
reason.not-recorded: {{tracker}} is not available yet: Agentry has not seen how {{cli}} answers, and builds nothing on something it has not seen.
reason.readyOwn: Reads and writes issues on {{host}} with {{cli}}, as {{user}}. It works in any project, whatever its code host.
reason.no-credentials: Give Agentry the address of your YouTrack and a permanent token to use it.
reason.token-rejected: {{host}} did not accept the token. Create a new one in your YouTrack profile, under Account security.
reason.host-unreachable: {{host}} did not answer. Check the address, and that this machine can reach it.
reason.notInstalledOwn: {{cli}} is not installed, or Agentry cannot find it. It is JetBrains' program for YouTrack, installed with npm.

bin.title: {{cli}} binary for {{tracker}}
bin.hint: Left empty, {{tracker}} uses the same program as {{host}}. If you choose another, Agentry reads its version before saving it and checks it is not older than {{minimum}}.
bin.usePath: Use the one of the host

binOwn.hint: Left empty, Agentry looks for {{cli}} on the PATH. If you choose another, Agentry reads its version before saving it and checks it is not older than {{minimum}}.

credentials.title: Access to YouTrack
credentials.hostHint: Your instance's address, such as https://acme.youtrack.cloud, or https://example.com/youtrack when it lives under a path.
credentials.tokenHint: Create it in YouTrack, in your profile under Account security, with the YouTrack scope. Agentry hands it to youtrack-app only through its environment and never shows it again.
credentials.tokenSaved: Saved · leave it empty to keep it
credentials.encrypted: Kept encrypted with this computer's keyring.
credentials.plain: Kept in a file only this server's user can read.
credentials.savedNotReady: Saved, but YouTrack is not ready: {{reason}}
credentials.forgotten: Agentry forgot the access to YouTrack
credentials.failed: Could not save the access to YouTrack
credentials.loadFailed: Could not read the access to YouTrack
